learning_outcomes.text: Knows distributions of one-dimensional random variables and their cumulative distribution functions.
Knows definitions and properties of random variable parameters.
Knows basic concepts of statistics. Principles of estimation and hypothesis testing.

Able to select an appropriate probabilistic model for a given problem. Proficiently uses density and cumulative distribution functions to calculate probabilities and random variable parameters. Applies the theorem on functions of continuous random variables. Applies limit theorems. Able to process a sample, determine confidence intervals, and test parametric hypotheses.
Applies density and cumulative distribution functions to calculate probabilities. Determines random variable parameters.
Determines distributions of functions of continuous random variables.
Able to process a sample, test parametric hypotheses, and determine confidence intervals for mean and variance.
Applies limit theorems to solve given problems.
Able to work in a group. Able to use scientific materials. Able to present prepared information.

syllabus_topics: Probability theory: Data analysis methods. Basic probabilistic models. Descriptive statistics and exploratory analysis. Visualization of measurement data.

Probability theory basics, Random variables and their distributions. Parameters of random variables. Continuous and discrete distributions. Limit theorems. Applications of random variable distributions in engineering practice.
Mathematical statistics basics. Estimation and statistical inference.
Introduction to multivariate methods. Modern statistical methods.
Probability theory: Descriptive statistics, preliminary data processing, probability theory;
Random variables, distributions of random variables, probabilistic models;
Correlation and regression; significance tests of the correlation coefficient;
assessment_rules: Students participate in lectures, learning subsequent teaching content according to the course syllabus, and should ask questions and clarify doubts as they arise. Audiovisual recording of the lecture requires the instructor's consent. For auditorium classes, students are required to prepare for exercises as indicated by the instructor (e.g., in the form of problem sets). Student work may be assessed based on oral or written statements in the form of a colloquium, which, in accordance with AGH study regulations, contributes to the final grade for this form of class.
